state.description: Flow lifecycle state. 'active' is the default. Reducer enforces transitions per common-fields.md §5.1: cx.flow.archive MUST come from 'active' (else failed_precondition reason=flow_not_active); cx.flow.restore MUST come from 'archived' (else flow_not_archived); terminal state is reached only via a cx.redaction event targeting the flow (MUST come from {'active','archived'} else flow_already_terminal). Same-state self-transitions MUST fail. 'redacted' is the irreversible terminal.

state_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent state transition. MUST be set when state != 'active'; MUST be the created_at of the corresponding cx.flow.archive / cx.flow.restore / cx.redaction Event. Aligns with Space.state_changed_at and the common-fields rule in models/common-fields.md §3.

tracks.description: Active Flow tracks, keyed by track name. Tracks are pure section pointers (synthesis vs discussion timeline) — they do NOT carry independent membership / permissions / history visibility / E2EE. Any sub-Realm-level access scoping MUST be modelled as a linked Realm referenced via 'discussion_realm_ref'. At most one track entry may explicitly set is_primary=true; when none does, the reducer derives the primary track by the deterministic rules in models/flow-and-message.md §4.5. The map MUST contain at least one entry; track names are validated by propertyNames.

discussion_realm_ref.description: Optional reference to a linked Realm that hosts this Flow's discussion-side membership, history visibility, and (if E2EE) MLS group. Setting this field means the discussion lives in its own security boundary distinct from the Flow's source Realm. When unset, discussion timeline events live in the source Realm and inherit its access.

flow_track.description: Flow track entry — a pure section pointer (synthesis vs discussion timeline). The track's stable name is the map key in Flow.tracks; this object holds the track's per-entry config. Tracks do NOT carry independent membership / permissions / history visibility / E2EE. To give the discussion side its own security boundary, set Flow.discussion_realm_ref to a linked Realm.
